newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Medical April sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Medical April sales rise.

text.p: Integrated Medical Resources Inc said Friday April revenues increased from March, as the company focuses on increasing the number of patients it serves.
The company, which provides impotence treatment and services at its 31 clinics, said revenues in April were about $1.62 million, up 10.2 percent from March.
"This year we are focused on improving same-store performance and increasing the number of patients seen at the centers," Troy Burns, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.
The company reported on Friday a first quarter loss of $1.84 million versus a profit of $21,000 last year.

IMR said it cut costs in the first quarter compared with fourth quarter, with center expenses down 18.6 percent, advertising costs off 17.5 percent ot $1.36 million and sales, general and administration costs trimmed by seven percent.
It said while last year the company developed 17 new clinics, this year it is focused on improving the results of those clinics.

"Our highest priorities are improving the number of patients seen, enhancing revenues from our existing patient base, testing the addition of new services for our patients, and developing additional research revenue," T. Scott Jenkins, president and chief operating officer, said.

"In addition, we are marketing ourselves and our services to potential physician referral sources, aligning and integrating urological leaders into the company and physician staff, and beginning to market ourselves to payers," he said.
